lines.trans: From my days as a salesman, words have always been my weapon.
The power of spoken words is extraordinary.
Together with you, I want to create an unscripted world.
Oh, how beautiful—please take a look.
It is no exaggeration to call this breathtakingly beautiful!
Your director is hilarious, isn't he!

words.gloss: be known (in かもしれない)

lines.trans: He came back stronger than ever.
Hey, you guys are ramping up mass production too, right?

words.gram: Colloquial contraction of だろう after past tense た.

lines.trans: Yes, and we will be counting on your stores when we do.
I am relieved we can distribute approved titles normally now too.
It is your fault for making the industry king get dead serious.
If he isn't serious, crushing him wouldn't be nearly as satisfying.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'sales'.

examples.text: これからセールスに行きます。
examples.trans: I'm going out on sales calls now.

examples.text: セールスの仕事は大変です。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: セールスをやっていた私の武器は言葉です。
examples.trans: From my days as a salesman, words have always been my weapon.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Noun.

examples.text: 新しい言葉を覚えました。
優しい言葉をかけてくれた。
examples.trans: She spoke kind words to me.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: 彼の英語は本当にすごい。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: 私はあなたと予定調和ではない世界を作りたいんです。
examples.trans: Together with you, I want to create an unscripted world.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: More formal counterpart of じゃあ used in business and polite conversation.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Used for the physical world or a specific sphere/industry (この世界).

examples.text: この世界に入る覚悟はあるか。
examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').
I-adjective describing beauty.

examples.trans: Mama, you're looking beautiful today too.

examples.text: ああ美しい、ご覧ください。
examples.trans: Oh, how beautiful—please take a look.

examples.text: 皆様、どうぞとくとご覧くださいませ。
examples.trans: Everyone, please take a good, close look.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Compound ichidan verb formed from する + すぎる.

examples.text: 最近働きすぎています。
examples.trans: I've been working too much lately.

examples.text: 心配しすぎないでください。
俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

examples.text: 美しすぎるといっても過言ではないでしょう！
examples.trans: It is no exaggeration to call this breathtakingly beautiful!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite presumptive form of copula だ; with rising intonation, seeks agreement.

examples.text: 明日は晴れるでしょう。
examples.trans: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Ichidan verb; most commonly appears in the set expression かもしれない ('might be').

examples.text: 遅れるかもしれません。
本当かもしれませんよ。
examples.trans: It might be true, you know.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: おもしれえじゃねえか、お宅の監督。
examples.trans: Your director is hilarious, isn't he!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.trans: He came back stronger than ever.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Godan intransitive verb.

examples.text: 仕事に戻って稼いでくれ。
examples.trans: Go back to work and earn money.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.en: sentence-final particle of emotion or reflection
meanings.note: Colloquial particle expressing sighing, wishing, or emphasis.

examples.text: いいなあ、うらやましい。
制作費はこれまでの五倍かけて量産していくぞ！
examples.trans: We will spend five times our previous budget and mass-produce!
Hey, you guys are ramping up mass production too, right?

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').
Core adverb in set greetings like よろしくお願いします and どうぞよろしく.
With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

examples.text: 正規の作品も扱えるようになって安心しました。
examples.trans: I am relieved we can distribute approved titles normally now too.

examples.trans: I am relieved we can distribute approved titles normally now too.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: お前らがポルノ王を本気にさせたのが悪いんだぞ。
examples.trans: It is your fault for making the industry king get dead serious.

examples.text: 日本のポルノ王を逮捕。明日の新聞の見出しはこれで埋まる。
examples.trans: Japan's industry king arrested—tomorrow's newspaper headlines will be filled with this.

meanings.en: bad; sorry (in past 悪かった)
meanings.note: Casual past 悪かったな admits fault ('that was bad of me / my bad').

examples.text: 今日は天気が悪いです。
本気じゃないと潰しがいがありませんよ。
examples.trans: If he isn't serious, crushing him wouldn't be nearly as satisfying.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
